summary: This document revises the tcpControlBits IPFIX Information Element, originally defined in RFC 5102, to reflect changes to the TCP flags header field since RFC 793. It was later replaced by RFC 9565.

eli5.summary: TCP packets carry little on/off switches. This updates a measuring form so it can record all the switches that exist today. It has since been replaced by RFC 9565.

questions: how does ipfix record tcp flags
what are the ecn flags in tcp
what is reduced-size encoding in ipfix
subtitle: Updates the IPFIX tcpControlBits field so flow records can carry all the TCP flags in use, including ECN.

tldr.problem: The IPFIX tcpControlBits Information Element only covered the six TCP flags from RFC 793, so it could not be used to measure ECN or match the current TCP Flags field.
tldr.mechanism: It redefines tcpControlBits as an unsigned16 bit field that covers the NS, CWR and ECE flags as well, with rules for the Data Offset bits, the Future Use bits and reduced-size encoding.
tldr.outcome: Collectors can now see ECN-related flags in flow data, but must treat old zero values for CWR and ECE with care. RFC 9565 has since replaced this document.

today: RFC 7125 is Informational and has been obsoleted by RFC 9565, which now carries the current definition.

sections.title: Why the Definition Needed Revising
sections.content:
Octets 12 and 13 of the TCP header hold the data offset (header length) in 4 bits and 12 bits of flags. RFC 793 defined the least significant 6 of these: URG, ACK, PSH, RST, SYN and FIN. RFC 3168 then added CWR and ECE for Explicit Congestion Notification (ECN), and RFC 3540 added NS for the ECN Nonce Sum.

The tcpControlBits Information Element came from RFC 5102 and only covered the original six bits. To let IPFIX measure ECN use and match the current TCP Flags field, it had to change.

Because RFC 5102 is a Proposed Standard, revising the element needs IETF consensus. The new definition was approved through the IE-DOCTORS process in August 2013, and publishing this RFC supplies the consensus.
sections.eli5: TCP packets have little flags, like flags on a mailbox. The old form only had space for six of them, but there are more now, so the form needed more room.

sections.title: The Revised Information Element
sections.content:
The element has ElementId 6, data type unsigned16 and data type semantics flags. It reports the TCP control bits seen across the packets of a Flow: a bit is set to 1 if any observed packet of the Flow had that TCP bit set to 1, and cleared to 0 otherwise.

The bit values run from 0x0100 for NS down to 0x0001 for FIN, covering CWR, ECE, URG, ACK, PSH, RST and SYN in between. The three bits 0x0800, 0x0400 and 0x0200 are Future Use, and the top four bits are zero.
sections.eli5: The record keeps a row of switches. A switch is turned on if any packet in the conversation had it on.

sections.title: Zero, Future Use and Reduced-Size Encoding
sections.content:
The most significant 4 bits of the field overlap the TCP data offset. They MUST be exported as zero and MUST be ignored by the collector; the tcpHeaderLength element carries the header length instead. The 3 Future Use bits SHOULD be exported as observed in the TCP headers.

An Exporting Process may use reduced-size encoding, exporting a single octet that covers bits 0x80 to 0x01. That omits the NS bit and the three Future Use bits, and a collector must not assume anything about their content. If the Metering Process cannot observe those bits, the exporter SHOULD use reduced-size encoding.
sections.eli5: Some boxes on the form are not used, so they must be left blank. If a counter cannot see some switches, it may send a shorter form with only the switches it can see.

sections.title: Compatibility with Earlier Exports
sections.content:
Earlier revisions of the definition said that the CWR and ECE bits must be exported as zero, even if observed. So collectors should not assume that a zero for these bits means they were never set, especially if they are zero in every Flow Record from a given exporter.

IANA updated the registry entry, setting the revision to 1 and the revision date to the publication date.
sections.eli5: Older forms always showed two of the switches as off, even when they were on. So if you see them off on an old form, you cannot be sure.

sections.title: Size Change and Security
sections.content: The change moves the element from unsigned8 (1 octet) to unsigned16 (2 octets). Because Exporting and Collecting Processes use the Information Element Length field in Templates, Options Templates and reduced-size encoding rather than abstract type sizes, no impact on buffer sizing is expected. Otherwise the security considerations of IPFIX (RFC 7011) apply.
sections.eli5: The form got a bit wider, but the readers look at the size written on the form, so nothing breaks.

items.label: Zero
items.desc: Overlaps the data offset; see tcpHeaderLength.
